prompt:
In many countries, more and more people are buying goods online instead of in local shops.

Is this a positive or negative development?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: State clearly whether online shopping replacing local shops is positive or negative (or mainly one or the other)
Explain the positive side (for consumers, businesses, the economy)
Explain the negative side (for local shops, town centres, workers, the environment)
Support ideas with explanation and examples
Keep the judgement consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: Wider choice and easy price comparison save consumers money
Convenient for people with disabilities, rural residents or busy workers
Small producers can sell to customers worldwide through online platforms
Fewer trips by car to shopping centres
against: Local shops close, leaving empty high streets and fewer social meeting places
Jobs in retail are lost or replaced by insecure warehouse and delivery work
Packaging waste, returns and delivery vans increase environmental impact
Customers cannot see or try products, and personal advice disappears

models.text:
Over the past decade, online shopping has grown from a convenient extra into the main way many households buy everything from books to groceries. Although this shift offers consumers undeniable benefits, I believe it is a mixed development that becomes negative when it hollows out local shopping streets.

From the consumer's point of view, the advantages are considerable. Online retailers offer a far wider range of products than any physical shop could stock, and customers can compare prices in seconds, which keeps costs down. For people with limited mobility, those living in rural areas without nearby shops, or parents with little free time, home delivery can make daily life significantly easier. The internet has also lowered barriers for small producers: a craftsman in a remote village can now sell to customers on the other side of the world through online marketplaces.

However, these gains carry costs that are less visible but equally real. As sales move online, many local shops lose the customers they need to survive, and when they close, town centres decline. Empty shopfronts discourage visitors, which harms the surrounding cafés and services in turn. Local shops also play a social role; a neighbourhood greengrocer or bookshop is a place where people meet and where elderly residents may have their only conversation of the day. Moreover, the jobs created in large distribution warehouses are often more repetitive and closely monitored than traditional retail work. Environmental impacts must also be considered, since individually packaged deliveries and the high rate of returned items generate substantial waste and traffic.

On balance, I see online shopping as positive when it complements local commerce, but negative when it replaces it entirely. Local governments can help maintain a balance by reducing business taxes for independent shops and turning town centres into attractive places to spend time rather than merely to buy.

In conclusion, online shopping brings choice, savings and convenience, yet its unchecked growth threatens the economic and social life of local communities, which makes it, overall, a development to be managed with care.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): posición clara y matizada ('mixed... becomes negative when it hollows out local shopping streets'), coherente en todo el texto y concretada en un párrafo de valoración. Ventajas y desventajas desarrolladas desde varias perspectivas (consumidores, productores, comunidad, empleo, medio ambiente). Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión lógica con cadenas de causa-efecto ('when they close, town centres decline... which harms...'); conectores bien integrados. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('hollows out', 'lowered barriers', 'shopfronts', 'greengrocer', 'unchecked growth', 'complements'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras complejas variadas (relativas, comparativas, pasivas) sin errores. Para un 9: una postura algo más tajante o mejor anclada (un caso real de un centro urbano en declive) y algo más de concisión en el párrafo de desventajas.

models.text:
Nowadays, many people prefer to buy clothes, electronics and even food on the internet instead of going to local shops. In my opinion, this trend has some important advantages, but overall it is a negative development for our towns and cities.

On the one hand, online shopping is very convenient for customers. People can buy products at any time of the day without leaving their homes, which is especially useful for busy workers and for elderly or disabled people who find it difficult to go out. In addition, websites offer a much wider choice of products than local shops, and customers can easily compare prices to find the cheapest option. For example, when I bought my laptop, I compared prices on several websites and saved almost a hundred euros.

On the other hand, there are serious disadvantages. The main problem is that many small shops cannot compete with large online companies, so they are forced to close. As a result, town centres become empty and less attractive, and people lose places where they used to meet their neighbours. Furthermore, many shop assistants lose their jobs. Online shopping is also bad for the environment, because every product is delivered separately in a box, which creates a lot of packaging waste and more traffic from delivery vans.

In my view, these negative effects are more important, because they affect the whole community, not only individual customers.

In conclusion, although online shopping is convenient and often cheaper, I believe it is a negative development because it damages local businesses, town centres and the environment. People should try to support local shops whenever possible.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): postura clara y justificada con un criterio ('affect the whole community, not only individual customers'), lo que es un buen recurso; ejemplo personal concreto (el portátil). El párrafo de valoración es muy breve y podría desarrollarse más. Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara; conectores correctos pero previsibles ('On the one hand', 'In addition', 'On the other hand', 'As a result', 'Furthermore'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('convenient', 'compete', 'packaging waste', 'delivery vans'), con alguna expresión general ('bad for the environment', 'a lot of'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control de estructuras ('are forced to close', 'used to meet'); errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: ampliar el párrafo de valoración, usar léxico más preciso ('high street', 'environmental footprint') y variar la forma de introducir los argumentos.

models.text:
Today, the online shopping is very popular. Many people buy clothes, books and electronic things in internet, for example on Amazon, and they don't go to the shops of their city. In my opinion, this is a positive development but it has also some negative points.

Firstly, online shopping is very comfortable. You can buy everything from your sofa and you don't need to go out, especially when it is raining or very cold. Also, in internet you can find more products and the prices are cheaper than in the shops. For example, last month I bought some shoes online and they were thirty percent cheaper than in the shop in my street. Also, the package arrive to your house in one or two days, so it is very fast.

Secondly, online shopping is good for the people who don't have time. Many people work all the day and when they finish the shops are closed. With internet they can buy at night or in the weekend.

However, there are some negative points. The small shops lose customers and some of them have to close. This is sad because the streets are empty and the shop owners lose their business. Also, the delivery produce a lot of boxes and plastic, and this is bad for the environment.

In conclusion, I think that online shopping is positive because it is comfortable, cheap and fast. But the people should also buy in the local shops sometimes to help them, because if not, all the small shops will disappear.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): postura clara ('positive'), pero la conclusión recomienda apoyar a las tiendas locales para que no desaparezcan, lo que matiza la postura sin haberlo desarrollado. Ideas relevantes pero generales; los dos primeros párrafos del cuerpo repiten la misma idea (comodidad). Coherence & Cohesion (6): enlace mecánico ('Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Also' repetido tres veces); el segundo párrafo no aporta una idea nueva. Lexical Resource (6): falso amigo 'comfortable' (convenient); 'electronic things', 'very fast', 'sad'; 'the prices are cheaper' (prices are lower). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'the online shopping' (sin artículo), 'in internet' (on the internet), 'the package arrive to', 'the delivery produce', 'all the day', 'in the weekend' (at/on), 'has also' (orden). Para subir a 7: agrupar las ventajas para evitar repeticiones, explicar por qué lo positivo pesa más, cuidar los falsos amigos y las preposiciones con internet.

prompt:
Some people say that individuals can do very little to fight climate change, and that only governments and large companies can make a real difference.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: State clearly how far you agree that individuals can do very little
Discuss the role and power of governments and large companies
Discuss what individuals can (or cannot) achieve
Support each main idea with explanation and examples
Keep the position consistent and restate it in the conclusion

for: A small number of energy, transport and industrial companies produce most emissions
Only governments can pass laws, set carbon taxes and fund clean infrastructure
Individual choices are limited by what is available and affordable (e.g. no public transport)
One person's emissions are tiny compared with national totals
against: Millions of individual choices together are significant (diet, flying, energy use)
Consumer demand pushes companies to change (electric cars, plant-based food)
Citizens vote, protest and pressure governments (e.g. youth climate movements)
Individuals influence family, friends and workplaces, spreading new norms

models.text:
Faced with the scale of climate change, many people feel that recycling a bottle or switching off a light is a meaningless gesture, and that the real responsibility lies with governments and corporations. I agree that these institutions have by far the greatest power to cut emissions, but I disagree that individuals can do very little, since their choices and, above all, their political actions shape what those institutions do.

There is no doubt that structural change is essential. A relatively small number of energy, transport and manufacturing companies account for a large share of global emissions, and only governments can introduce carbon taxes, phase out coal power or invest billions in rail networks and renewable energy. Individual effort is also constrained by circumstances: a commuter who lives in a town without public transport may have no realistic alternative to driving, however concerned they are about the environment.

Nevertheless, it would be a mistake to conclude that individuals are powerless. First, their combined consumption is substantial. In wealthy countries, decisions about how often to fly, how much meat to eat and how to heat a home make a measurable difference when multiplied across millions of households. Second, consumer demand sends signals to businesses. The rapid growth of electric vehicles and plant-based foods has been driven partly by customers who wanted greener options, and companies have responded because it is profitable to do so.

Most importantly, individuals are also citizens. Governments rarely take unpopular decisions unless voters demand them, and public pressure, through elections, petitions and protests, has repeatedly pushed climate policy up the political agenda. The school strikes that began in Sweden in 2018, for example, started with a single student and grew into a global movement that influenced political debate in many countries.

In conclusion, although governments and large companies hold the main levers of change, individuals are far from insignificant. Through what they buy, how they live and, crucially, how they vote and campaign, they help determine whether those levers are ever pulled.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): posición matizada y precisa (de acuerdo en que gobiernos y empresas tienen más poder, en desacuerdo con que los individuos puedan hacer 'very little'), clara desde la introducción y mantenida. Tres argumentos bien desarrollados (consumo agregado, demanda, presión política) y un ejemplo concreto (huelgas escolares de 2018). Coherence & Cohesion (8): estructura impecable con gradación ('First', 'Second', 'Most importantly'); la metáfora de las palancas une introducción y conclusión. Lexical Resource (8): léxico preciso ('structural change', 'phase out', 'constrained by circumstances', 'sends signals', 'political agenda', 'hold the main levers'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): estructuras complejas variadas ('however concerned they are', 'Governments rarely take... unless', pasivas) sin errores. Para un 9: alguna cifra o dato aún más concreto sobre emisiones y un párrafo de concesión con un matiz adicional (p. ej., el riesgo de que las empresas trasladen la responsabilidad al consumidor).

models.text:
Climate change is one of the biggest problems facing the world today. Some people argue that ordinary people cannot do much to solve it and that only governments and big companies can make a difference. I partly agree with this view, but I believe that individuals also have an important role to play.

On the one hand, it is true that governments and large companies have much more power than individuals. Governments can make laws to reduce pollution, for example by banning petrol cars or taxing companies that produce a lot of carbon dioxide. They can also invest in renewable energy, such as solar and wind power, and in public transport. Similarly, large companies, especially in the energy and manufacturing sectors, produce a huge amount of emissions, so if they change their methods, the impact is much bigger than anything one person can do.

On the other hand, individuals can still make a difference. If millions of people use public transport, eat less meat and save energy at home, the total effect is significant. In addition, customers can influence companies through what they buy. For instance, as more people want electric cars, car manufacturers are producing more of them. Finally, individuals can vote for politicians who take climate change seriously and join campaigns to put pressure on the government.

In conclusion, I agree that governments and big companies can do the most to fight climate change, because they have the power to make large-scale changes. However, I do not agree that individuals can do very little, since their daily choices and their votes can encourage these institutions to act.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): responde a la pregunta con una postura comprensible y argumentos relevantes; sin embargo, 'I partly agree' en la introducción es menos preciso que la conclusión, y el argumento político (votar, campañas), quizá el más fuerte, aparece al final con muy poco desarrollo. Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clara; conectores correctos pero previsibles ('On the one hand', 'Similarly', 'On the other hand', 'In addition', 'Finally'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('renewable energy', 'emissions', 'large-scale', 'put pressure on'), con expresiones algo generales ('a lot of', 'much bigger'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control (condicionales, 'as more people want...'), errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: precisar la postura desde la introducción, desarrollar el argumento político con un ejemplo concreto y usar léxico más específico ('carbon tax', 'phase out').

models.text:
Nowadays, the climate change is a very big problem for all the world. Some people think that one person can not do nothing and only the governments and the big companies can change the situation. I partly agree with this opinion.

Firstly, the governments and the companies are more powerful than the people. The companies have big factories that produce a lot of pollution, for example the oil companies and the car companies. If one company reduce the pollution, it is more important than if one person recycle the plastic. Also the governments can make laws, for example they can prohibit the old cars in the city centre or give money for the solar panels. One person can not do this.

Secondly, I think that the people also can help a little bit. For example, we can use the bicycle or the bus and not the car, we can recycle and we can switch off the lights when we don't use them. If everybody do this, the pollution will be less. In my family we always recycle and we use the public transport.

However, sometimes it is difficult for the people to help. The electric cars are very expensive and in some villages there is not public transport, so the people need to use the car. For this reason, the government must to help the people with money.

In conclusion, I think that the governments and the big companies are more important to fight the climate change, but the people also can do some things. If all of us work together, we can save the planet.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): responde a la pregunta con una postura ('partly agree') y argumentos pertinentes, pero generales; no menciona cómo los individuos influyen en gobiernos y empresas (voto, demanda), el argumento más fuerte contra la afirmación. El ejemplo familiar es anecdótico y la conclusión es un tópico ('we can save the planet'). Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura identificable pero mecánica ('Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Also', 'However'); el tercer párrafo cambia de dirección sin enlace claro con la postura. Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico ('a very big problem', 'a little bit', 'more important'); falta léxico temático ('emissions', 'renewable energy'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'can not do nothing' (doble negación), 'If one company reduce', 'if one person recycle', 'If everybody do', 'there is not public transport' (there is no), 'must to help', 'the climate change' (sin artículo). Para subir a 7: añadir el papel de los ciudadanos como votantes y consumidores, desarrollar cada idea con un ejemplo real y revisar negaciones y concordancia en condicionales.

prompt:
Some people believe that scientific research should be paid for mainly by governments. Others think that private companies should be responsible for funding it.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

Write at least 250 words.
checklist: Discuss the view that governments should mainly fund scientific research
Discuss the view that private companies should fund it
Give your own opinion clearly and consistently
Support both views with reasons and examples
Give the two views roughly equal attention

for: Governments can fund basic research with no immediate profit (e.g. physics, space, climate science)
Public funding keeps research independent and results openly available
Some areas serve the public good but are unprofitable (rare diseases, vaccines for poorer countries)
Governments can support long-term projects that companies would abandon
against: Companies have large budgets and reduce the burden on taxpayers
Commercial pressure turns discoveries into useful products quickly
Private funding can be more efficient and less bureaucratic
Companies that profit from research should pay for it

models.text:
Scientific research drives medical progress, technological innovation and economic growth, but it is expensive, and there is considerable debate about who should pay for it. While private companies clearly have a valuable role to play, I believe governments should remain the main funders, particularly of fundamental research.

Those who favour private funding make several reasonable points. Large technology and pharmaceutical companies have research budgets that rival those of entire countries, and relying on them reduces the burden on taxpayers. Commercial pressure can also be productive: because firms need to bring products to market, they tend to move quickly from discovery to application, as the rapid development of several vaccines during the recent pandemic showed. Furthermore, it seems fair that companies which profit from new knowledge should contribute to the cost of producing it.

However, there are strong reasons why research cannot be left mainly to the private sector. Companies naturally invest in projects likely to generate a return within a few years, whereas many of the most important discoveries come from basic research whose practical value is unclear at first. Investigations into the behaviour of electrons or the genetics of bacteria, for instance, eventually made possible modern electronics and gene-editing technologies, but no business would have funded them at the outset. Similarly, areas that serve the public good but promise little profit, such as treatments for rare diseases or tropical illnesses that mainly affect poorer countries, would be neglected. There is also the question of independence: when research is funded by a company with a commercial interest in the outcome, results may be withheld or presented selectively, as has happened in the tobacco and fossil fuel industries.

In my view, the most effective system is one in which governments fund basic and public-interest science, while companies concentrate on developing applications, ideally in partnership with universities.

In conclusion, both public and private funding contribute to scientific progress, but because only governments can support long-term, independent and unprofitable research, they should continue to bear the main responsibility.
models.commentary: Task Response (8): discute ambos puntos de vista con equilibrio y profundidad y da una opinión clara (los gobiernos deben ser los principales financiadores, sobre todo de la investigación básica) que se mantiene y concreta en un modelo mixto. Ejemplos específicos y bien elegidos (vacunas, electrones, genética bacteriana, industrias del tabaco y combustibles fósiles). Coherence & Cohesion (8): progresión impecable; 'However, there are strong reasons why...', 'Similarly', 'There is also the question of independence' articulan el argumento con naturalidad. Lexical Resource (8): léxico académico preciso ('rival', 'bring products to market', 'at the outset', 'public-interest', 'withheld', 'presented selectively', 'bear the main responsibility'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (8): gran variedad de estructuras (relativas con 'whose', condicional 'would have funded', pasivas) sin errores. Para un 9: algo más de desarrollo del modelo de colaboración propuesto y un tono aún más conciso en el párrafo central, que es muy largo.

models.text:
Scientific research is essential for the development of society, but it is also very expensive. Some people think that governments should be responsible for paying for it, while others believe that private companies should provide most of the money. This essay will discuss both views before giving my own opinion.

On the one hand, there are good reasons why private companies should fund research. Many large companies, such as technology and pharmaceutical firms, earn huge profits, so they can afford to invest in science. If they pay for research, governments can spend more taxpayers' money on other important areas, such as education and healthcare. In addition, companies usually work efficiently because they want to sell new products as soon as possible. For example, smartphone companies spend billions on research every year, and this has led to rapid improvements in technology.

On the other hand, many people believe that governments should be the main source of funding. Companies only invest in research that can make money, so some important areas may be ignored. For instance, research into rare diseases is often not profitable, because few people suffer from them. Moreover, research paid for by companies may not be objective. A company might hide results that are bad for its products, which could be dangerous for the public.

In my opinion, governments should pay for most scientific research, especially in areas like medicine and the environment, because these affect everyone. However, companies should also contribute, particularly to research that is closely connected to their products.

In conclusion, although private companies can fund research efficiently, I believe that governments should take the main responsibility, because they can support research that benefits the whole of society rather than only making a profit.
models.commentary: Task Response (7): discute ambos puntos de vista con ideas relevantes y da una opinión clara y coherente. Falta el argumento de la investigación básica a largo plazo (sin aplicación inmediata), que haría la postura más convincente; algunos ejemplos son generales ('smartphone companies'). Coherence & Cohesion (7): estructura clásica bien ejecutada; conectores correctos pero algo previsibles ('On the one hand', 'In addition', 'On the other hand', 'Moreover'). Lexical Resource (7): vocabulario adecuado ('afford', 'taxpayers' money', 'profitable', 'objective'), con alguna expresión simple ('bad for its products'). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (7): buen control de estructuras complejas (pasivas, condicionales, 'rather than'); errores casi inexistentes. Para subir a 8: incluir el argumento de la investigación fundamental con un ejemplo concreto, desarrollar más la idea de la independencia con un caso real y usar léxico más preciso ('withhold results', 'conflict of interest').

models.text:
Science is very important for the world because it help us to find new medicines and new technologies. But science research need a lot of money. Some people think the government must pay for it, but other people think that the private companies should pay. In this essay I will discuss both opinions.

Firstly, some people think the government should pay for the research. The government has the money of the taxes and it should use this money for things that are good for all the people, like the science. Also, if the government pay, the scientists can investigate what they want and not only what is good for the business. For example, the investigation about the climate change is very important but the companies don't want to pay for this because they don't win money.

Secondly, other people think that the companies should pay. The companies have a lot of money, for example Google or Apple, and they can invest in new technologies. When the companies pay for the research, the government can use the money for other things like hospitals and schools. Also the companies work more fast than the government because they want to sell the products.

In my opinion, I think both should pay for the research. The government should pay for the research that is important for all the society, like medicine and environment, and the companies should pay for the research of their products.

In conclusion, the government and the companies both have advantages to pay for the science research. I think the best is that they work together for make more discoveries.
models.commentary: Task Response (6): discute los dos puntos de vista y da una opinión (ambos deben pagar), pero con ideas generales y poco desarrolladas. El ejemplo de Google y Apple sólo dice que tienen dinero, sin conectar con el argumento. Coherence & Cohesion (6): estructura correcta, pero 'Firstly' y 'Secondly' introducen puntos de vista, no argumentos; 'Also' se repite y la conclusión es confusa ('both have advantages to pay'). Lexical Resource (6): vocabulario básico ('a lot of money', 'good for all the people'); falsos amigos frecuentes en hispanohablantes: 'investigation/investigate' (research), 'win money' (make/earn money), 'science research' (scientific research), 'the money of the taxes' (tax revenue). Grammatical Range & Accuracy (6): errores frecuentes: 'it help us', 'science research need', 'if the government pay', 'more fast' (faster), 'for make' (to make), 'In my opinion, I think' (redundante), artículos innecesarios ('the science', 'the climate change'). Para subir a 7: desarrollar cada punto de vista con un ejemplo que demuestre el argumento, eliminar falsos amigos ('research' en lugar de 'investigation') y revisar concordancia y comparativos.
